## Legion: class halls and artifacts

### Artifacts

- **[Fix]** Core/Items: artifact weapons are equipped on receipt in their scenario.
- **[Fix]** Core/Items: the off-hand of a two-piece artifact weapon is kept when swapping.
- **[Fix]** DB/Quests: artifact weapon choice panels show their real artwork (demon hunter, warrior, mage).
- **[Fix]** DB/Quests: artifact weapon choice panels read in French.

### Class halls

- **[Fix]** DB/Quests: class campaign quests are limited to their class.
- **[Fix]** Core/Quests: class hall scouting map (option shown, zones taken, window closed).
- **[Fix]** DB/Order halls: the original repack's acolytes no longer offer every campaign quest a second time.
- **[Fix]** DB/Quests: Dalaran class calls after the arrival and class couriers summoned before their quest, for every class.
- **[Fix]** DB/SpellArea: Dalaran phases, quest-bound auras apply in the right quest states.
- **[Fix]** Core/Scenarios: class scenarios on maps shared by several classes (demon hunters no longer get the hunter's in the Violet Hold).
- **[Fix]** Scripts/Artifacts: the Dreadblades scenario is registered on its map; Felo'melorn's Violet Hold is registered.

*The artifact scenarios below received fixes; they have not all been played through to the end yet.*

## Security

- **[Change]** **Passwords are stored as Argon2id hashes** (needs OpenSSL 3.2+); old SHA-256 hashes still work and are converted at the first successful login.
- **[Exploit]** **Progressive wrong-password blocking:** the IP address, then the account, with increasing durations (`WrongPass.BanSteps`), reset after `WrongPass.ResetTime` or a successful login. A banned IP gets no web login ticket, a second ticket on an authenticated session is refused, a client stalling in the TLS handshake is dropped after 2 s.
- **[Exploit]** RA passwords are masked in the log; `Ra.IP` defaults to 127.0.0.1.
- **[Exploit]** **Network hardening:** an exception in a socket handler no longer ends the process; an account with no session key, an early encryption confirmation and an unvalidated instance key are refused.
- **[Exploit]** **Client packets are checked** (range, ownership, state) for items, trade, void storage, toys, movement, taxi, chat, who, calendar, tickets, quests, NPCs, queries, professions, spells, pets, artifacts, authentication, account, garrison, challenge mode, duels, scenes and loot (master loot could give an item to a player on another map).
- **[Exploit]** Element counts and strings sent by the client are bounded before any allocation; character screen requests are refused while a character is in the world; a client without a character can only queue a few delayed packets; spell projectile data and Warden lengths are bounded.
- **[Exploit]** Characters: ownership checks, asynchronous rename, undelete cooldown; one open ticket per account.
- **[Crash]** Client packets above 64 KB cut the connection (hotfix requests past about 5,700 hotfixes); the limit is 256 KB.
- **[Change]** zlib updated to 1.3.1 (security fixes).

### Progression and rewards
_`Everything in this section is a deliberate departure from the official game, not a restoration of it. The realm reopens Legion tier by tier, and these settings exist to make that pacing hold.`_
⠀
- `Game.Patch` takes one value per Legion patch (7.0 → 7.3) instead of three.
- Item levels are pinned server-side instead of read from the client: dungeons at 805 / 825 / 840 for the whole expansion, raids attached to their own map, Karazhan per boss. The client's DB2 data holds the 7.3.5 catch-up values, which were inflated at the end of the expansion to let latecomers skip ahead. Using them made a normal dungeon out-reward the first raid.
- Mythic+ loot follows the key up to +25, where the original game stopped at +15. It stays capped by the heroic raid of the open tier, so a high key never out-rewards unreleased content.
- Creature scaling is computed from two tunable slopes instead of the client tables: 8% per key up to +15, 5% above. A +15 is worth 2.72x and a +25 4.43x. The client's own tables would put that same +25 at 9.85x: they rise by 10% compounded per key and never flatten.
- Artifact Knowledge advances per character through the class hall order again, capped by tier (25 / 40 / 55). The realm used the late 7.3 design: one world state bumped weekly and forced onto every character at login, which leaves no individual progression at all.
- A Knowledge book drops from current-tier raids, the Mythic+ chest and PvP chests: free-for-all, one per player per week. Off by default.
- A catch-up quest rerolls an alt to rank 10, gated on a new account-wide condition type.
- The weekly chest has its own item level cap.
- The per-tier item level penalty that still applied to dungeon loot is gone, now that dungeon levels are pinned.
- Legion Assaults and the pre-patch invasions get their own options, independent of the patch level.

- **[Damage variance system]** Carried over from 9.x. Minimum and maximum damage are computed from a variance that falls back to 0.3466 when the client data is missing or zero, and every hit swings ±5% either way.
  > `Damage.Variance.Pct` sets the spread, and 0 makes every hit deterministic again. It sits on top of the weapon's own min/max damage, which only spreads weapon swings.

### Performance

- The send buffer is only built when there is something to send, instead of being zeroed for every player every millisecond, almost always for an empty queue.
- `Map.NumThreads` at 1 runs inline, instead of paying the queue handoff and the condition variable wait for a single worker that brings no parallelism.
- An instanceable map with no instance idles instead of spinning for the rest of the uptime.
- Creatures keep their ground height until they move, instead of walking two spatial trees every update.
- Creature spell lists become a vector — 100k templates paid for a bucket array to hold 8 spells.
- Map lookups move to unordered containers, and the pull cell size is read once rather than on every pull.
- The DAMAGE_BUG diagnostic drops from error to debug, so it stops hitting the disk on every low-damage hit.
